entries.063fce3296876086: In its core tugboat business, the company implemented a revision of tugboat rates in May 2025 to match rising costs, and states that going forward it will pursue efficiency through reducing operating crew complements, optimizing fleet size, and introducing an AI-based vessel deployment support system. On the environmental front, drawing on knowledge gained from operating the hybrid electric propulsion tugboat that entered service in 2023, the company states that it aims to introduce pure battery tugboats by around 2030. For its offshore wind power business, which it intends to grow as one of its core businesses, the company states that in addition to crew transfer vessels (CTV), it will work on business development for SOVs and other vessels and on training of seafarers. In the passenger ship business, Tokyo-wan Ferry plans to replace vessels through bareboat charters of newly built ships, starting in autumn 2027.
entries.0921943d5ada2efc: Its main customers are operators of vessels entering and leaving Tokyo Bay, businesses that construct and maintain offshore wind power facilities, and passengers using the car ferries.
entries.0957d707d4099afe: In the tugboat business, it provides tugboat services that assist large vessels in berthing and unberthing and operates pilot boats; in the maritime-related business, it operates and charters crew transfer vessels (CTV) for offshore wind power generation; and in the passenger ship business, it operates car ferries linking Kurihama and Kanaya.
entries.3179a4799d401d28: This is a business model in which the company, centered on tugboat services, operates maritime-related businesses such as operation of crew transfer vessels (CTV) for offshore wind power generation, and passenger ship businesses such as car ferries, and earns revenue from service fees for operations and passenger fares.
entries.34aceb692dd6a670: This business centers on operating crew transfer vessels (CTVs) that carry offshore wind power workers to generation facilities at sea, and also includes in-port crew transfer boat services, charter services for owned vessels, and the maritime disaster prevention business.

entries.5395f37760d5d6a3: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥13,144 million, broken down into ¥9,517 million from the tugboat business, ¥1,956 million from the maritime-related business and ¥1,670 million from the passenger ship business.
entries.60c212d9df24c851: Of revenue of ¥13,144 million for the fiscal year ended March 2026, the tugboat business accounted for ¥9,517 million (about 72.4%), the maritime-related business for ¥1,956 million (about 14.9%), and the passenger ship business for ¥1,670 million (about 12.7%), with the tugboat business accounting for the majority.
entries.62bc94f643607638: This business is operated by consolidated subsidiary Tokyo Wan Ferry Co., Ltd., which runs car ferries connecting Kurihama Port in Kanagawa Prefecture and Kanaya Port in Chiba Prefecture. It also includes shop and restaurant operations at the ferry terminals. Sightseeing boat operations at Yokohama Port have been handled since May 2025 by equity-method affiliate YCruise Co., Ltd.
entries.650a50cee3edab46: This business centers on operating crew transfer vessels (CTVs) that carry offshore wind power workers to generation facilities at sea, and also includes in-port crew transfer boat services, charter services for owned vessels, and the maritime disaster prevention business. The company and consolidated subsidiary Port Service Co., Ltd. handle this business.
entries.6536cdbf4687d224: The group's tugboats are engaged in escort services for vessels in the Uraga Channel and Nakanose Fairway, berthing and unberthing assistance for vessels at ports across Tokyo Bay, guard vessel services at LNG berths and other locations, disaster prevention work, and emergency dispatch and maritime rescue, and the structure is characterized by supporting the safe navigation of vessels across the whole of Tokyo Bay.
